Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
news.story: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times.…

Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati.
news.story: Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option…

news.headline: Freiermuth (illness) is active for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
news.story: The Steelers added Freiermuth to their Week 10 injury report Saturday due to an illness, which left him questionable for Sunday. Now that he's confirmed to be available, he'll look to bounce back from a mostly dry spell before the team's Week 9 bye, when he caught exactly two passes in three consecutive contests without a touchdown after scoring four TDs through the first five weeks of the campaign.

news.headline: Freiermuth (illness) was added to Saturday's injury report and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Cincinnati.
news.story: Freiermuth is battling through an illness, which puts the veteran tight end's status for Sunday's AFC North tilt in jeopardy, and his official status may not be known until the Steelers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. If Freiermuth cannot play, then Robert Tonyan would step into a larger role offensively alongside Darnell Washington, and tight end…

news.headline: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
news.story: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

news.headline: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
news.story: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

news.headline: Singletary is expected to return to a change-of-pace role Thursday against the Commanders, as Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation.
news.story: Singletary recorded a season-high 23 touches in Skattebo's absence during the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 but mustered only 39 yards with all that volume. Prior to that win, Singletary hadn't exceeded six carries in a game this season. Skattebo is expected to lead the backfield in his return, with Singletary likely to feature in passing situations since Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) remains on IR. Greg…

news.headline: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
news.story: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

news.headline: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that "there is not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) will suit up Sunday at Denver, but the tight end is "pushing to play."
news.story: Bowers was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury. Head coach Klint Kubiak labeled Bowers day-to-day last Monday, and he then missed Wednesday's practice before being limited Thursday and Friday and entering the weekend listed as questionable. It appears Bowers' availability will be subject to a pregame warmup, after which his status will be…

news.headline: Bowers (ankle) said Friday that his availability for Sunday's game against the Broncos remains up in the air, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
news.story: "We still have some conversations to have, so we'll see," Bowers said. With the tight end already slated to carry a questionable tag into the weekend, his own comments don't provide added clarity about whether he'll suit up Sunday. The Raiders may wait until closer to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff before making a final call on Bowers' status. Jack Bech was the big winner in terms of playing time and targets after Bowers…

news.headline: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit…

news.headline: Likely didn't practice Friday due to a strained groin, but he doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Jaguars, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.
news.story: There was some worry about the breakout tight end's status for Week 11 when he wasn't spotted at Friday's session, but head coach John Harbaugh allayed some of those fears, telling Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com that Likely was dealing with a "minor thing" and should be good to play Sunday. With no designation in tow, Likely is in the clear and probably is set for his typical 8.9 targets per game.

news.headline: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Likely is tending to a "minor thing" but should be good to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports.
news.story: Likely appears poised to go down as a non-participant on the final practice report of this week due to an undisclosed injury. A designation ahead of Week 11 action thus seems likely for the tight end, which will become known later Friday.

news.headline: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
news.story: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

news.headline: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
news.story: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25…

news.headline: Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

news.headline: Douglas (shoulder) is expected to play Sunday against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
news.story: Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.story: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. news.story: Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive…

news.story: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. news.story: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. news.story: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard…

Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.
news.story: With Bam Knight back in the lineup in Week 10 after one absence due to a concussion, Allgeier didn't reach double-digit touches for the first time since Week 5, a span in which the latter's 65 touches went for 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Knight himself found a similar lack of success Sunday with just 19 yards on his five rushes. Because the Cardinals racked up just 123 yards of offense in rookie QB…

news.headline: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
news.story: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and…

Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
news.story: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas…

news.headline: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
news.story: The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

news.headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
news.story: Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited…

news.headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
news.story: Rodriguez was listed on injury reports both of the past two weeks due to the hand issue, but he proceeded to suit up for wins against the Ravens and Titans and handled his usual backup duties behind lead back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot). Assuming his limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related and not the result of any setback, Rodriguez should be ready to play Sunday against the Giants.

Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
news.story: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for…

Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
news.story: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019…

news.headline: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.
news.story: Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6…

news.headline: Burks (foot) did not practice Friday.
news.story: The Commanders have been managing Burks' practice reps, as he deals with a foot injury that's been nagging him for several weeks. He missed practice time last week but still was able to play against the Giants last Thursday, securing two of three targets for 27 yards. Washington will provide final injury designations Saturday ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

news.headline: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants.
news.story: Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production…

news.headline: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.
news.story: In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

news.headline: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
news.story: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time…

Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
news.story: Washington finished second in receiving yards for the Dolphins and also was partly responsible for the team's one score through the air, uncorking a well-thrown 34-yard strike to Jalen Tolbert on a trick play. Washington also continued to produce in his returner role, and he's now up to 812 all-purpose yards through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

news.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
news.story: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

news.headline: Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
news.story: The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

news.headline: Kolar (concussion) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice.
news.story: The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

news.headline: Kolar (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
news.story: Kolar led the Chargers in snaps at tight end (41) during Monday's game at Baltimore, but it appears he may have suffered a concussion at some point during the contest. He'll need to progress through the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, which includes gaining clearance from an independent neurologist, before he'll be allowed to return to game action. His level of activity at practice Thursday or Friday could…

Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
news.story: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

news.headline: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt…

news.story: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching…

Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
news.story: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
news.story: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

news.headline: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
news.story: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

news.headline: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
news.story: Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

news.headline: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
news.story: The Jaguars have often kept Meyers limited early in the week since the veteran suffered an ankle injury, but he has yet to miss a game this year. There have even been weeks when Meyers did not practice Wednesday but still ended up playing. As it stands, Meyers' status will be worth monitoring for the rest of the week, but limited midweek work has been the norm for him.

news.headline: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
news.story: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too…

news.headline: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
news.story: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck…

news.headline: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.

news.headline: Knight (concussion) practiced in full Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
news.story: Knight was limited Wednesday after donning a yellow non-contact jersey in practice, but after ditching it one day later, he was able to handle every on-field rep. That's not to say he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires an evaluation from an independent neurologist, but he's likely on the precipice of doing so. Friday's injury report will determine if Knight heads into the weekend with a…

news.headline: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
news.story: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively.…

news.story: That said, Duggan noted that he did see Likely, who hasn't been on the Giants' Week 11 injury report so far, walking into the building after the team's Friday morning walkthrough. In any case, New York's upcoming practice report will provide context regarding Likely's apparent absence, as well as his official status for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

news.headline: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
news.story: The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

news.headline: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
news.story: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11…

news.headline: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
news.story: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo…

news.headline: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
news.story: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

news.headline: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
news.story: There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top fantasy RB play.

news.story: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

news.story: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

news.story: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

The veteran wideout could immediately slide into a major role in Arizona's passing game among a depleted wideout corps that has lost Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) for the season. Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
news.story: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

news.headline: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
news.story: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both…

news.headline: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
news.story: Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season…

news.headline: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
news.story: Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

news.headline: The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday.
news.story: It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change…

news.headline: Blue was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
news.story: Blue was let go by the Eagles after suiting up for the team in Weeks 8 and 9, a span in which he didn't record a carry and caught his only target for nine yards. Now that he's back on the team's practice squad, the 2025 fifth-rounder will give Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley-led RB corps an added depth option ahead of Week 11 action.

news.headline: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
news.story: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers,…

news.headline: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
news.story: A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday…

news.headline: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
news.story: The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.

news.story: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. news.story: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

news.headline: The Giants signed Jones to their practice squad Wednesday, Dan Salomone and Matt Citak of the team's official site report.
news.story: Jones was waived from the Giants' active roster Monday, but after going unclaimed, he's decided to stay with the organization as a member of the practice squad. Over six games with the G-Men so far this year, he's caught two of three targets for 66 yards while also returning some kicks and punts.

news.headline: The Giants waived Jones on Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
news.story: Jones has mostly operated on special teams for the Giants and has appeared in six regular-season games, with his two catches (on three targets) for 66 yards all coming in Week 6 against the Saints. Jones will now go on waivers, and though he'll have the chance to explore his next options if he goes unclaimed, he may opt to stay with the Giants as a member of the practice squad.

With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

news.story: Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

news.story: Allen looked rejuvenated in his 49ers debut after coming over from the Colts at the deadline, finishing third in receptions and receiving yards and second in targets for his new squad in the wild win. news.story: Allen could have a significant role immediately, joining an injury-riddled WR room, though Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been cleared to play this Sunday. news.story: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

news.headline: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
news.story: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

news.story: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. news.story: Monangai told Courtney Cronin of ESPN on Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints, and after being spotted in full pads at Tuesday's unofficial practice, the running back would have logged an uncapped session one day later if the team had held drills. Monangai is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a turf toe injury and a right thumb concern.

news.headline: Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports.
news.story: A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the…

news.headline: Restrepo was signed to the Titans' active roster Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official website reports.
news.story: Restrepo was elevated to the active roster in Week 10 against the Jaguars, and he reeled in all three of his targets for 31 yards over 19 offensive snaps. After fellow wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Restrepo will replace him on the active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cowboys.

news.headline: Restrepo reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday.
news.story: After being elevated ahead of Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars, Restrepo finished with three receptions for 31 yards. The wide receiver played 19 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. Restrepo can be elevated on more occasion before the Titans would need to add him to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play.

news.headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
news.story: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the…

news.headline: Fantasy buzz: Does anything change in Indy with Richardson under center?
Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
news.story: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break…

news.headline: Evans (Achilles) is reportedly ready to return to action Sunday night against the Vikings, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
news.story: Evans, who hasn't played since Week 6, logged limited practices Thursday and Friday before heading into the weekend listed as questionable, but in an Instagram post, the wideout's agent relayed that Evans is set to return versus Minnesota on Sunday. This nugget is good news for those considering Evans in Week 11 fantasy lineups, but his status is nonetheless worth verifying ahead of the 49ers' 8:20 pm ET kickoff.

news.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status…

news.headline: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
news.story: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

news.headline: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
news.story: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most…

news.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
news.story: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

news.headline: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
news.story: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11…

news.headline: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation.
news.story: After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.

news.headline: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday.
news.story: Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully and thus avoid an injury designation prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

news.headline: McConkey (back) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Jets, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
news.story: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and then was inactive in Week 10, is officially listed as questionable by the Chargers after logging limited practices all week. While the wideout is on track to return to action versus New York, those considering McConkey in Week 11 fantasy lineups are still advised to verify his status once inactives are posted ahead of Sunday's 4:05 pm…

news.headline: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
news.story: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers'…

news.headline: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
news.story: McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

news.headline: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.
news.story: Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders…

news.headline: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
news.story: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in…

news.headline: Njoku (fibula) officially is listed as active for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
news.story: Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season,…

news.headline: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.
news.story: After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during the week of practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for Monday's game. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar likely will lead the position group in…

Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.
news.story: Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

news.headline: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
news.story: Tyson maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a chest injury in the wake of his 11-80-0 line on 13 targets from the second game of his career this past Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

news.headline: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
news.story: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo…

news.story: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

news.headline: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
news.story: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits…

news.headline: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
news.story: Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again…

news.headline: Conklin went without a target while playing 22 of the Lions' 71 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
news.story: A healthy inactive for two of the Lions' first four games of the season, Conklin has now suited up for five consecutive contests. However, the veteran tight end has been handling a limited role, logging less than one-third of the offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances on the season while compiling a 2-11-0 receiving line on three targets.

news.headline: Traore went without a target while playing six of the Dolphins' 69 snaps on offense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
news.story: Meanwhile, Traore tied a season-high with 23 snaps on special teams, where he continues to receive the bulk of his playing time. The reserve tight end has played in all nine of the Dolphins' games to date but has gone without a reception while being targeted once across 39 total snaps on offense.

news.headline: Baker Mayfield's 58-yard dime sets up Bucky Irving's TD for Bucs
Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
news.story: Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand…

news.headline: Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
news.story: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of…

news.headline: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
news.story: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week…

news.headline: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
news.story: Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and…

news.headline: Long (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
news.story: Long was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the sixth-year pro has been cleared to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He will operate in a rotational role at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.

news.headline: Arizona activated Long (knee) from injured reserve Saturday, and he remains questionable for Sunday's battle against the Rams.
news.story: Long had been on IR since Oct. 6 after suffering a knee injury during Week 4 against the Giants. He was limited in all three of the Cardinals' practice sessions this week but could suit up Sunday. If Long plays, he'll work as a depth tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, though Long could still have some pass-catching opportunities given how depleted the team's wideout corps is.

news.headline: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
news.story: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

news.headline: Week 10 winners and losers: McCaffrey, Gibbs and Mahomes dominate Sunday
Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. He added one rushing yard on his only carry.
news.story: Chuba Hubbard did most of the heavy lifting on offense for the Panthers, piling up 172 scrimmage yards and both the team's touchdowns. It's the first time this season Young failed to throw a TD, but it was also the first time since Week 6 he avoided committing a turnover. The fourth-year QB will take a 16:6 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash against the Ravens.

news.headline: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
news.story: Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season…

news.headline: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
news.story: Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

news.headline: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
news.story: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too…

news.headline: Hawes (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.story: Hawes' practice reps during Week 11 prep were limited by a shoulder injury, which he may have picked up during the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. Dalton Kincaid (thumb) is listed as doubtful, so that leaves Dawson Knox and Keleki Latu as the two healthy tight ends on the Bills' 53-man roster heading into the weekend. If Hawes is cleared to play, then he would operate as the TE2 behind Knox in the event that…

news.headline: Hawes (shoulder) was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News.
news.story: It is unclear whether Hawes suffered his shoulder injury, however, his eligibility for Week 11 against the Dolphins will likely be decided during the Thursday and Friday prep sessions. The 25-year-old will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

news.headline: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
news.story: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

news.headline: Tate (shoulder) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
news.story: Tate, who hasn't played since Week 7, had been listed as questionable for the contest despite being a full practice participant Friday. Now that he's back after missing Tennessee's last two games, in the absence of any in-game setbacks or limitations, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft should immediately reclaim a prominent role in the team's offense in a plus matchup, with his addition to the lineup…

news.headline: Tate (shoulder) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
news.story: After turning in a pair of limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Tate upgraded to full participation to close the week, and he then headed into the weekend with a 'questionable' designation. However, per Rapoport, the wideout -- who last played in Week 7 -- is poised to rejoin the Titans' lineup, with his Week 11 status set to be officially confirmed, either way, before the first wave of games Sunday, with a…

news.headline: Tate (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys but is "considered likely" to be cleared to play, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
news.story: Tate drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after a full practice Friday, and all signs point toward the rookie fourth-overall pick returning from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. With Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle, IR) out for the rest of the year, Tate will lead a Titans wideout group that also includes Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, Xavier Restrepo and Calvin Ridley. Tennessee faces a Dallas defense Sunday…

news.headline: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
news.story: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each…

news.headline: What to know to set your lineup: Nix, Ward viable options if your QB is on bye
Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
news.story: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

news.headline: Bellinger caught two of three targets for six yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
news.story: The blocking specialist played 28 of 57 offensive snaps and was asked to block on 12 of those plays. His two-yard touchdown in the second quarter was Bellinger's first of the season. For the year, Bellinger has 11 grabs for 76 yards and the score on 18 targets across nine contests.

news.headline: Schoonmaker (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
news.story: Schoonmaker was held out of practice Thursday and Friday due to an illness, and he's drawn the questionable tag heading into the weekend. Jake Ferguson (knee) has already been ruled out, and with Schoonmaker under the weather, that leaves Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the Cowboys' two healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's contest. Michael Trigg could be elevated from the practice squad…

news.headline: Schoonmaker caught one of two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers.
news.story: Schoonmaker garnered a season-high two targets, but he failed to produce his first multicatch performance of the year. The tight end played 28 offensive snaps in contest, ranking second at his position behind Brevyn Spann-Ford (55) and ahead of James Mitchell (five). With Jake Ferguson (knee) expected to remain sidelined in Week 11, Schoonmaker will have another chance to operate as the team's top reserve option at…

news.headline: The Cowboys signed Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
news.story: The Cowboys technically still have one elevation to use on Mitchell this season, but they instead will opt to sign him to the active roster for Week 10. His signing gives the Cowboys extra depth at tight end, as the team will be without Jake Ferguson (knee) for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

news.headline: Wright caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
news.story: Wright tied season highs in both receiving yards and catches during Sunday's win, and his 39 snaps on offense were second-most among Lions tight ends behind Sam LaPorta (56). Wright has accumulated seven catches on eight target for 42 yards across nine regular-season games, and he's mostly served as a blocking tight end on the Lions' offense.

news.headline: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.
news.story: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

news.headline: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers.
news.story: In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

news.headline: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
news.story: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time…

news.headline: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
news.story: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a…

news.headline: Gadsden (eye) returned to Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Gadsden was poked in the eye in the first quarter and had to go to the locker room before returning early in the second quarter. He wasn't targeted in the passing game prior to sustaining the injury.

news.headline: Gadsden (eye) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Ravens.
news.story: It's unclear when Gadsden suffered the injury, but he went to the locker room midway through the first quarter. He wasn't targeted prior to leaving the contest. David Njoku and Charlie Kolar will handle tight-end duties for the Bolts while Gadsden is sidelined.

news.story: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11…

news.story: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. news.headline: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports.
news.story: McCarthy missed much of the third quarter of this past Sunday's win at Philadelphia due to a hip pointer but was able to return to action, completing 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing four times for 22 yards. Considering he ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, he seemingly was in the clear for Thursday's matchup, and Palmer's report indicates McCarthy will…

news.headline: Evans (Achilles) is reportedly ready to return to action Sunday night against the Vikings, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
news.story: Evans, who hasn't played since Week 6, logged limited practices Thursday and Friday before heading into the weekend listed as questionable, but in an Instagram post, the wideout's agent relayed that Evans is set to return versus Minnesota on Sunday. This nugget is good news for those considering Evans in Week 11 fantasy lineups, but his status is nonetheless worth verifying ahead of the 49ers' 8:20 pm ET kickoff.

news.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status…

news.headline: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
news.story: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

news.headline: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
news.story: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this…

news.headline: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.
news.story: Jennings opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP listings due to a calf injury and now will miss his second contest of the campaign. With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

news.headline: Jennings (calf) did not participate at practice Thursday.
news.story: Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

news.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) is slated to be activated from IR in time to play in Monday's game against the Bengals, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
news.story: Croskey-Merritt has missed the Commanders' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury. news.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Bengals.
news.story: Croskey-Merritt logged a full week of practice since the Commanders designated him for return from injured reserve Tuesday, which generally is a good sign he'll return to action Monday. Meanwhile, fellow RB Rachaad White was limited Friday and didn't practice Saturday due to a heel issue, also leaving him questionable for Week 11 action. The team will need to activate Croskey-Merritt from IR by Monday afternoon for…

news.story: Head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Saturday that Croskey-Merritt had a "great week" of practice. The second-year running back has missed the Commanders' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury, but it appears as though he'll be activated from IR ahead of Monday's contest. news.story: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. news.story: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
